lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Under King Darius the Mede, Daniel rose again to the highest rank. And the satraps hated him for it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They searched for something — anything — to accuse him of. But they found no fault. Not one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So they built a trap from the one thing they could not take from him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A new law: for thirty days, anyone who prays to anyone but the king is thrown to the lions.

choices.label: Daniel closes his window 🪟
choices.note: He didn't. They couldn't find fault in him by catching him pray — so the window was always open.

choices.label: Daniel prays as usual ✅
choices.note: Three times a day. Window open. Facing Jerusalem. Exactly as he always had. Because that's what faithfulness looks like.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel went home. He opened the window facing Jerusalem. He got down on his knees. And he prayed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three times a day. Just like always. Not as a protest. Not to make a point. Simply because it was time to pray.

lines.speaker: darius
lines.text: I cannot reverse my own law. I'm so sorry, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel was thrown in. The stone was sealed. And Darius paced his palace all through the long night.

lines.speaker: darius
lines.text: DANIEL! Servant of the living God — has your God been able to save you?!

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: O king, live forever. My God sent his angel, and the lions' mouths were shut. Because I was found innocent before him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel was lifted out. Not a scratch on him. Because he had trusted in his God.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Daniel prospered. Under Darius. Under Cyrus. Through four kings and two empires — seventy years of exile — he held the line.

consequence.god_only: And Daniel prospered. Under Darius. Under Cyrus. Through four kings and two empires — seventy years of exile — he held the line, unbent and unbroken.
consequence.mixed: And Daniel prospered. Under Darius. Under Cyrus. Through four kings and two empires — seventy years of exile — he held the line, faithful despite the compromises.
consequence.compromised: And Daniel prospered. Under Darius. Under Cyrus. Through four kings and two empires — seventy years of exile — he held the line, a pragmatic path but a faithful one.

consequence.god_only: THE END — Conviction sustained across seven decades, unbroken.
consequence.mixed: THE END — Faithfulness threaded through with compromise, but the line held.
consequence.compromised: THE END — A different kind of faithfulness, but faithful nonetheless.
